BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE 1.

The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as PFA Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of the Da vs Rajender Prasad on 9 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101620588/
1 PFA Act and Rules.
2.

Initially, after conclusion of the trial, accused was convicted by the then Ld. ACMM vide order dated 06.02.2014 under section 16(1)
(a) of the PFA act read with section 7 of the PFA act, for violation of rule 29 and was accordingly sentenced.
3. Thereafter, the accused had challenged the order of conviction and sentenece before the appellate court.

The Ld. ASJ-04 had set aside the order of conviction and sentence vide order dated 08.02.2023 and remanded back the case with the following observations:
"...15.

It is clear and evident that the issue that the primary evidence in the form of sign board was not produced and its effect thereof, was not decided by the Trial Court, in view of its erroneous observation that the CFL analysed the sample on the basis of standard meant for fruit drink, whereas, the CFL has clearly examined the sample on the basis of standard meant for thermally packed fruit juice contained in A.16.06.
16.Secondly, the point urged before me that A.16.06and A.16.10 deals with thermally processed and packed product and perhaps A.16.30 deals with non-thermally processed fruit drink and whether or not there is a provision akin to A.16.01 of the unamended provision, is an issue which has not been gone into by the Trial Court,
more specifically, when there is nothing on record to indicate that the sample seized was thermally processed product.

Ld. SPP is also not able to point, at this ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR Date:
2024.02.09 16:58:51 +0530 Cr. Case 1998/2023 Delhi Administration Vs.
Rajender Prasad
. Page No. 2 of 11 stage, at least, that there is any material to show a claim that the product seized was thermally processed.

17.In these circumstances, order of conviction and sentence cannot be sustained and is liable to be set aside and matter remanded back to the Trial Court to hear arguments on these aspects afresh, record additional evidence, if required, and give conclusive finding.
4. Accordingly, arguments were heard afresh at length on behalf of the accused and the department.
Furthermore, none of the parties requested or filed any application for adducing any additional evidence.
5. In the course of arguments, the defence counsel limited their contentions to the assertion that the accused was selling artificially flavoured fruit drink, not fruit juice.
Additionally, the counsel argued that the standard outlined in Rule 16.06 for thermally packed juice was not applicable to the present facts and circumstances of the case.

Da vs Rajender Prasad on 9 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101620588/
2 6.

The counsel continued to expound on the arguments, highlighting that after the sample was lifted,
the accused expressed concerns to the department, specifying that the sample was a fruit drink and not fruit juice.
This communication, including the letter addressing this concern, is a documented part of the record.
Moreover, during the cross-examination of witnesses, the defence suggested that the sample was a fruit drink.

In light of this, the counsel emphasised that the prosecution was under an obligation to present on record the board seized from the shop, which constitutes primary evidence, to ABHISHEK by ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR
Delhi Administration Vs. Rajender Prasad.
Page No. 3 of 11 substantiate its claim that the accused was selling fruit juice and prosecution has failed to establish this obligation.
7. The counsel has strongly emphasised on the point that the sample lifted could not be classified as a thermally processed drink.
Hence, the application of standard required under rule 16.06 by Director, RFL was incorrect.

Furthermore, there was no available standard in the rules, which could have been applied on the lifted sample and coloring material including tartizine was permissible upto 200 ppm as per co-joint reading of the rule 29 and rule 30, which in the instant case was below the permissible limit.

8. On the contrary, the learned Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) argued that the witnesses examined in court have unequivocally testified that the signage board prominently displayed "pineapple juice artificially flavored."
All witnesses, according to the SPP, have consistently corroborated this point.

Additionally, Form No. VI, which describes the sample, also indicates the same description and bears the thumb impressions of the accused, who was explained the contents in Hindi during the sample seizure.

The SPP refuted the defence argument, asserting that there was no necessity to produce the signage board in the court record since the proceedings were conducted by public servants and there is no evidence on record discrediting the testimonies of the witnesses.
Hence, the prosecution contends that it is firmly established that the sample was fruit juice.
Digitally signed by ABHISHEK ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR
Delhi Administration Vs. Rajender Prasad.
Page No. 4 of 11 9.
The learned SPP further asserted that the correct standard, 16.06, was aptly applied to the pineapple juice sample.
The SPP contended that the presence of tartizine, a coloring material, was impermissible in any fruit juice or drink, thereby conclusively establishing the culpability of the accused.

10. Before proceeding further, it is pertinent to refer to the facts of the case and the evidence available on record.
11.

The case of the prosecution is that on 17.12.2008 at about 3:00 p.m, Food Inspector Suniti Kumar Gupta and Field Assistant Ashok Kumar ,under the supervision and directions of SDM/ LHA Sh. M.S. Vats visited at M/s NU Look Pvt. Ltd., Shop No. 20, Regal Buldg., Connaught Place, New Delhi-110001, where accused Rajender Prasad who was the vendor-cum manager /nominee was found selling Pineapple Juice, for sale for human consumption.

Da vs Rajender Prasad on 9 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101620588/
3 12.

Further, the Food Inspector collected/purchased the sample of Pineapple Juice which was sent to Public Analyst for analysis and as per the report of Public Analyst, the sample was adulterated because it was found "coloured with synthetic colouring matter "Tartrazine".

Thereafter,
Sanction/Consent under Section 20 of the Act was obtained and the present complaint was filed for violation of provisions of Section 2 (i-a) (a) (j) & (m) of PFA Act 1954 as well as ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR
Delhi Administration Vs. Rajender Prasad.

Page No. 5 of 11 for violation of Rule 23 r/w Ruie 29 of PFA Rules 1955,
punishable U/s 16 (1A) r/w Section 7 of the Act.
13. After filing of the complaint, the accused was summoned vide order dated 17.07.2009.

Upon entering appearance, accused Rajender Prasad who also represents accused no. 2 i.e. M/s NU Look Pvt. Ltd., moved an application under Section 13(2) of PFA Act to get the second counterpart of the sample analysed from Central Food Laboratory.
Consequently, second counterpart of the sample as per the choice of the accused was sent to the Director, CFL (Pune) for its analysis vide order dated 30.07.2009.

The Director, CFL after analysing the sample opined vide its Certificate dated 18.08.2009 that "sample contains Total Soluble Solids less than 10.0%, Synthetic food colour i.e.
Tartrazine more than 100.00 ppm & hence does not conform to the standards of Fruit Juice as per P.F.A. Rules 1955 as per tests performed."
14.

Thereafter, matter proceeded for the recording of the pre-charge evidence and the prosecution had examined Food Inspector Suniti Kumar Gupta as PW-1 and pre charge evidence was closed vide order dated 20.10.2009.
The accused did not cross examine the witness despite opportunity.

15. Accordingly, vide order dated 15.12.2009, charge for the violation of provision of Section 2 (i-a)
(a) (j) & (m) of PFA Act 1954, ABHISHEK by ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR

Then, the matter was kept for post-charge evidence.

16. During post charge evidence, the prosecution had examined three witnesses including Food Inspector Suniti Kumar Gupta as PW- 1, SDM / LHA, Sh. M.S. Vats as PW-2 and Field Assistant Ashok Kumar as PW-3.
Thereafter, post charge evidence was closed vide order dated 31.03.2012.
The accused availed the opportunity to duly cross examine all the witnesses.
17. Then, the statement of the accused was recorded under section 313 CrPC and he did not lead any defence evidence despite opportunity being afforded.
Thereafter, the final arguments were heard and accused was convicted.
Now, after the directions of the appellate court, final arguments were heard afresh at length from both the parties.
18. Based on the evidence presented by the prosecution and the arguments presented in court, it is abundantly clear and uncontested that a food sample was collected and subsequently analysed.

sentences.text: Page  19.

As the accused has focused his arguments on the specific points discussed earlier in this order,
the findings will be provided to address those points specifically in the subsequent part of this order.
20. In the present case, the primary dispute raised by the accused is with regard to the description of the food sample lifted for analysis.

As per the prosecution, it was "Pineapple Juice (artificially flavoured)"
whereas accused has stated that it was not juice but "Pineapple Drink (Artificially flavoured).

The cornerstone to arrive at this conclusion is the signage board which was affixed at the shop of the accused and was ultimately seized by the raiding party,
which is evident from the testimonies of the witnesses.

The prime concern of the accused is that the signage board was never produced in the court and in its absence,
the fact whether sample was fruit juice or drink could not be established.

21. To counter the argument, the Ld. SPP has relied upon form no. VI which contain the details of the food, the contents of which were duly explained to the accused in Hindi and were acknowledged by the accused by putting his thumb impressions on the same.
Further, this fact stands corroborated through the testimony of PW1.

However, the counsel for the accused had argued that accused is illiterate and there is nothing written on form no. VI to substantiate the fact that the contents of the same were read over to the accused and it is also not mentioned in the complaint.
by ABHISHEK ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR
Delhi Administration Vs. Rajender Prasad.
Page No. 8 of 11 22.
After going through the file as well as form no. VI, one can easily notice that description of the sample is mentioned as "Pineapple Juice" and accused had received the copy of it.

It is also evident that accused had put his thumb impressions and the form no. VI does not bear anything to show that contents of the form were explained to the accused in Hindi barring the testimony of PW1 during trial which creates doubt with respect to the claim of the Food Inspector that contents were actually read.

This doubt further gets deeper when we take a close look at the document Ex. PW1/G & PW1/G1, which are the letters dated 18.12.2008 & 20.12.2008, addressed to the department where accused had raised the protest clarifying that sample lifted was fruit drink and not fruit juice,
Da vs Rajender Prasad on 9 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101620588/
5
which adds to the effort of the accused to show his bonafide of the claim.

23. Since, a doubt was raised with respect to the description of the sample as discussed above, it was essential for the department to have produced the signage board as primary evidence in the court or its photographs.
The description noted in form no. VI could only be considered as secondary evidence of the contents of the signage board.

Further, no reasons have been adduced by the prosecution as to why the signage board or its photographs were not produced in the court, which would have put end to the controversy regarding the description of the sample instantly.
The signage board in this case would have constituted as a document within the definition of evidence and was ABHISHEK by ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR

sentences.text: Page No. 9 of 11 required to be proved as per the mandate of section 65 of the Indian Evidence Act.
Further, the proof of the same does not fall under the exceptions enumerated under 65 of the evidence act.
Therefore, doubt regarding the description of the sample looms in the present case and the benefit of such doubt has to be extended to the accused.
24. Now, let's deal with the second set of the argument of the accused with respect to the incorrect applicability of standard 16.06 of the rules by the director RFL in assessing the sample.

25. After going through the rules and regulations and giving thoughtful consideration to the submissions of the parties, I have arrived at the conclusion that the standard of 16.06 pertains to the thermally processed packaged fruit juice and such standard could not have been applied to juice being loosely sold in the market or even to fruit drinks.

Further, use of the coloring material in fruit drink or fruit juice (artificially flavoured) as mentioned in the present case is squarely covered under rule 29 of the act and as such use of tartizine was permissible upto 200 ppm which in this case is 118 ppm, within prescribed standards.
There is no evidence on record to indicate that sample lifted was thermally processed.

Thus, finding of the expert with respect to the presence of coloring material Tartizine was not sufficient to arrive at the conclusion that accused has violated the provisions of the PFA act and that too, by applying standard 16.06 to ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR Date:
2024.02.09 17:00:06 +0530 Cr. Case 1998/2023
Delhi Administration Vs. Rajender Prasad.
Page No. 10 of 11 the sample, which appears to be incorrect on the basis of the description of the sample.
26. Accordingly, accused Rajender Prasad vendor cum nominee of M/s NU Look Pvt. Ltd, stands acquitted for offence under Section 16 of PFA Act.
27. Accused is directed to furnish personal bonds U/s 437A Cr.PC in the sum of Rs.10,000/-.
